To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Gα12, Gα13, and noncanonical Wnt pathways function together to regulate cell elongation and migration during convergence and extension movements in zebrafish.

1) Gα12 and/or Gα13 are essential for convergence and extension movements in zebrafish, and 2) Gα12/ 13 signaling is required for cell elongations underlying convergence and intercalation underlying extension.
Gα12/Gα13 are essential for cell elongation during convergence and mediolateral intercalation during extension, and that Gα12 is required for dorsalward migration during both processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying gastrulation movements in vertebrate development, which is a fundamental biological process that has been conserved from the invertebrates to mammals.
the mechanisms that regulate the development of the vertebrate body plan, in particular, how cells are patterned and move to form the body plan.
the role of G protein signaling in cell behavior and tissue morphogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Gα12 is involved in cell elongation during convergence, while Gα13 is involved in mediolateral cell intercalation during extension.
Gα12,13 signaling is essential in the convergence and extension movements of the gastrulation process in the zebrafish.
Gα12,13 signaling is essential in distinct cell behaviors during gastrulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Gα12/Gα13 signaling plays an important role in gastrulation by regulating cell behaviors that are essential for convergence and extension.
the Gα12/ 13 signaling pathway is required for cell elongations and cell migration during gastrulation.
Gα12/Gα13 are required for convergence and extension movements during zebrafis gastrulation, and Gα12/G13 function cell autonomously in distinct cell behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gα12 is essential for cell elongation during gastrulation, and that Gα13 has a redundant role in cell elongation.
